original_question: Let d be the Fubini-Study metric on the complex projective plane CP^2. Does there exist a sequence of nonnegatively curved polyhedral metrics d_n on CP^2 that converges to d?
target_in_paper: Section 8, "Faceting Fubini–Study": the paper asks whether the Fubini–Study metric on CP^2 can be obtained as a limit of nonnegatively curved polyhedral metrics on the same manifold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper extremely closely: it has the correct ambient manifold CP^2, the correct target metric d (the Fubini–Study metric), the correct class of approximants (nonnegatively curved polyhedral metrics), and the correct existence/approximation question. It is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the problem in Section 8. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
missing_details: The paper explicitly defines a polyhedral metric on a compact manifold as a length metric for which, with respect to some triangulation, every simplex is isometric to a Euclidean simplex. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))

The curvature condition is spelled out: "nonnegatively curved" means that the total angle around each codimension-two simplex is at most 2π; the paper states this is equivalent to nonnegative curvature in the sense of Alexandrov. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to say that each d_n is a metric on the same fixed compact manifold CP^2, not on a varying space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))

The paper leaves the mode of convergence implicit: it asks only whether d_n "converges to d." A stand-alone sharpening should therefore specify what convergence of metrics on the fixed manifold means. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
refined_question: Let d be the distance function of the Fubini–Study metric on the complex projective plane CP^2. Does there exist a sequence {d_n}_{n>=1} of polyhedral length metrics on the fixed manifold CP^2 such that, for each n, every simplex in some triangulation of CP^2 is isometric to a Euclidean simplex, the total angle around every codimension-two simplex is at most 2π (equivalently, d_n has Alexandrov curvature >= 0), and d_n(x,y) -> d(x,y) for all x,y in CP^2? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist a sequence {d_n}_{n>=1} of polyhedral metrics on CP^2 with Alexandrov curvature >= 0 such that d_n(x,y) -> d(x,y) for all x,y in CP^2, where d is the Fubini–Study metric? This uses exactly the equivalence stated in Section 8 between the codimension-two angle condition and nonnegative Alexandrov curvature. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: the relevant item is the unlabelled open problem in Section 8, "Faceting Fubini–Study," on page 5. The surrounding context on the same page provides the definitions of "polyhedral metric" and "nonnegatively curved," and immediately explains why the problem is specifically interesting on CP^2: such metrics are Kähler, and under a suitable parametrization their singular set is algebraic; the paper cites Panov for constructions and study of these metrics. I did not broaden the problem beyond CP^2 or beyond the nonnegatively curved polyhedral setting. The only genuine sharpening is that I made the paper’s implicit convergence clause concrete by writing it as convergence of the distance functions on the fixed underlying manifold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
